note: Passage 3701 (Pro 1:2-3) — the prologue: the aims of the book. Char-driven read; cognition acts (know/understand/receive) operate on the faculties + moral goods, each of which is also a characteristic (two-axes). Poetic mandatory ledger; none written explicit; locus=internal/external, coupling=the pairing.

dims.v: to know — the acquisition of wisdom as its aim
knowing wisdom and instruction — taking them into the inner person
paired with understanding (995) and receiving (part of one acquisition)
1:2 opens the book's purpose as an interior verb (know), not an act on the world; wisdom is gained by being known/received inwardly.
wisdom — the skilled, ordered competence of the inner life
wisdom as the faculty to be acquired and lived
paired with instruction (musar) — the disposition and its shaping named together
chokmah heads the list — the master good the book exists to impart; here it is the object of know (yada), the two-axes case (its own char AND know's target).
instruction as moral discipline — correction that shapes the inner person
the disciplining/shaping of the inner life to be received
welded to wisdom (chokmah) in the pair chokmah-umusar
musar = discipline received, not knowledge grasped — it carries the note of correction/shaping the inner life must submit to (distinct from wisdom's competence).
to understand — to discern the sense of words
paired with know (yada) — the two cognitive acts of the aim
bin (discern) is distinct from yada (know): it is the penetrating grasp of meaning, and its object is 'words of insight' — understanding applied to speech.
the discerning faculty by which words are understood
paired with understand (bin) — faculty and act of the same root
binah is the noun-faculty of bin; here it is the target of understand — the two-axes case again (faculty AND object).
instruction in wise dealing — discipline received, now specified by its fruit
receiving the discipline that produces prudent, upright conduct
welded to wise-dealing/righteousness/justice/equity — the moral goods it instils

musar recurs in 1:3 but now aimed at CONDUCT (wise dealing, righteousness, justice, equity) — the same discipline, its ethical output specified. Distinct occurrence, not a repeat of 264712 (which paired with wisdom-cognition).
prudent, insightful conduct — acting with skill in living
acting wisely/prudently in the conduct of life
paired with righteousness, justice, equity as the ethical triad it heads
sakal (prudent dealing) is conduct-competence, distinct from chokmah (competence as such) — it turns the inner good outward into right living, hence it heads the ethical triad of 1:3.
righteousness — rightness of the inner person toward the norm
the disposition to what is right, gained through discipline
tsedeq = rightness as a state of the person; distinct from justice (mishpat, right judgement/order) and equity (meshar, straightness) — the read keeps the three apart though they are listed together.
justice — right judgement and ordered dealing
discerning and rendering what is just
middle of the triad, with righteousness and equity
mishpat carries the note of judgement/verdict — the inner sense of right order that issues in fair dealing, distinct from tsedeq (rightness-as-state).
third of the triad, closing righteousness-justice-equity
mesharim (plural, 'straightnesses') = evenness/fairness — the level, undistorted dealing; distinct from mishpat's judgement and tsedeq's rightness. The prologue thus names three moral goods, not one.
